name: assay
use_label: Auto-check a web page for bugs
one_liner: Drives your web page in a real browser and tells you what broke.

text.why: Writing tests is a chore, so many changes ship unchecked. assay finds every control on the page, uses all of them, and reports what went wrong.
text.take: Because it needs no AI and gives repeatable results, it suits re-running after every fix.
build: It opens the page in Chromium and builds its checks from the controls it finds. If pressing a tag filter twice leaves the list filtered, it reports that with before and after views. No test code, no LLM, no API key, and every run gives the same result. A skill for coding agents is included.

who.role: Developers who want to check their own web pages before shipping.

start.text: Install with pip install assay-ui and run it on the address of the page you want to check.

caveat: Needs Python and Chromium. Recently released, with 98 stars.

license.scope_text: Use, change and redistribute, commercially too. Keep the notice.

numbers.star_delta_unit: GitHub stars gained in the window, GH Archive events summed to as_of
numbers.method: Star total = the value last checked on GitHub (stars_checked_at) + increases observed via GH Archive since. The 24h · 7d · 30d gains are GH Archive hourly events summed to the reference time (as_of). No score of ours.

images.alt: An assay result: a failure report that a tag filter pressed twice left the first click in effect, with before and after page views.

notes: This file was produced by the same build, from the same data, as the tesign.com item page. The text is editorial; the numbers are stored observations.
null in the JSON means not observed — never zero. The Markdown writes [unconfirmed] for it.
